criteria.criterion: athena.toml gains [capabilities.study] with producer_commands (no rm/mv/chmod wildcard, no network-capable commands such as git fetch, clone or curl), verifier_commands (read-only), checks, and env; it also names firstmate's repository URL and the ref to resolve, and holds no hand-typed SHA. athena.toml is named in this criterion as a governance-file change.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. athena.toml adds [capabilities.study] with producer_commands (cargo build/check/test/metadata/tree, git status/diff/log/show, ls *), read-only verifier_commands, fmt and test checks, and env. [capabilities.study.source] sets url = https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate and ref = "HEAD". There is no SHA anywhere. One caveat: `cargo build` and `cargo test` can download crates, but `change` grants them too.

criteria.criterion: A Capability hook with a default no-op body (so `change` is unchanged) lets the core call a capability when a job starts. Study implements it in Athena's Rust code, not in a prompt or producer command: it resolves the configured ref to a full 40-hex SHA, makes the tree available read-only, and records the SHA in the job's records and the producer's environment or brief.
criteria.evidence: Most of this is met. capability.rs adds `on_job_start` with a default that does nothing. Study's version in source.rs runs `git ls-remote`, checks for a full 40-hex SHA, fetches that commit, strips .git and makes the tree read-only at `<job_dir>/source`. The SHA goes into the brief (stored in the dispatch commit) and into ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA. But agents cannot reach the tree. agent_spec (reading.rs:111-116) sets the policy root to the snapshot (`<job_dir>/work` for the producer). policy.rs `evaluate` sends every Read/Grep/Glob/LS path through `confine`, which refuses anything outside root (policy.rs:423-426). So the pinned source is not available to the producer, even though the brief points it there.

criteria.criterion: The core invokes this hook in the job-start path, so a study job actually resolves and records the SHA. Nothing is left uncalled.
criteria.evidence: run.rs:192-197 calls `capability.on_job_start` in dispatch, before the producer brief is built. The brief note is appended to the brief (run.rs:216-219) and committed in the prediction commit. start.env reaches the producer (run.rs:406), and capability_env is reused for the checks and the verifier.

criteria.criterion: The producer prompt says the source is pinned, read-only and present, and that claims must cite the recorded full SHA. It has no other rewording.
criteria.evidence: producer.md changes one line, to "Source: pinned, read-only, present. Cite its recorded full SHA." Nothing else is reworded. The text matches the criterion, but in practice the claim that the source is "present" is false for the agent, because of the confinement noted under criterion 2.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md state that Athena resolves firstmate's SHA at study start, that the producer has no network, and that no SHA is hand-recorded. They do not say a user must add one.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG Added entry and D75 in decisions.md both say all three things. D75 cites the rejected attempt 20261012-211640-3x8m. Neither tells a user to add a SHA.

criteria.criterion: The reader's catalog lists `study` because its section is now in athena.toml. The wiring test for registered capabilities still passes. The study test that asserted the capability is absent from athena.toml is updated.
criteria.evidence: reading.rs:48/229/242 filter the catalog by `jc.config.capability(id).is_some()`, so `study` is now listed. The wiring tests pass, including the new every_registered_capability_has_a_section_in_athena_toml. The study test was renamed to the_verifier_never_writes_and_the_grants_come_from_athena_toml, and it now asserts the section is present.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. Offline tests, using an injected runner or a local fixture repository, cover: resolving a ref to a full SHA; rejecting a short, non-hex or empty result; rejecting an unresolvable ref; the hook being a no-op for `change`; and the hook being called at study start.
criteria.evidence: All tests pass. Covered: a_ref_resolves_to_a_full_sha, short_non_hex_and_empty_results_are_refused, an_unresolvable_ref_or_failing_remote_is_an_error, a_local_fixture_is_pinned_read_only, the_start_hook_does_nothing_for_change, and the_start_hook_resolves_pins_and_records_the_sha. Not covered: the hook being called at study start. No core test drives dispatch for a capability and checks that `on_job_start` runs or that its brief note and env arrive. Grep finds StartOutcome, brief_note and start_env only in capability.rs, run.rs and the two capability crates, with no core tests. The study test calls `pin_source` directly, so every test would still pass if the call in run.rs were removed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; both pass.
criteria.evidence: Both exited cleanly with no warnings or diffs.

findings.summary: The pinned source is outside the agents' confined working directory, so the producer cannot read it
findings.evidence: pin_source writes the tree to `<job_dir>/source`. The producer's policy root is the snapshot `<job_dir>/work`, and `confine` refuses any Read/Grep/Glob/LS path outside root with "resolves outside your working directory". The brief and the prompt tell the producer the source is present at that path. Every read of it would be refused, so a study cannot cite the source at all. Fix by placing or exporting the tree inside the snapshot (read-only, and excluded from the candidate) or by widening the read-only policy root.

findings.summary: No test shows that the core calls the hook at study start
findings.evidence: Criterion 7 requires a test for the hook being called at study start. The study test calls `pin_source` directly and the change test calls `Change.on_job_start` directly. No dispatch-level test (for example in tests/lifecycle.rs with a fake capability) checks that `on_job_start` runs or that its brief_note and env reach the brief and the agents. Removing the run.rs call would break no test.

findings.summary: The grant includes `cargo build`/`cargo test`, which can download crates
findings.evidence: cargo resolves dependencies over the network unless it runs offline. Agents have no network, so this is likely harmless, but the grant does not enforce it, for example with `--offline` or CARGO_NET_OFFLINE in env.

summary: Verdict: fail. The core does pin a SHA at study start, but the producer cannot read the pinned copy, and no test proves the hook is called. The study capability is now selectable, and Athena's own process resolves firstmate's ref with `git ls-remote`, checks it is a full 40-hex SHA, and fetches a read-only copy into the job directory. It records the SHA in the dispatch-committed brief and in ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA. The docs, prompt and config match the request. The test suite, clippy and fmt all pass (I ran them). Two problems remain. First, a blocker: the copy goes to `<job_dir>/source`, but the agent tool policy only lets the producer read inside its snapshot (`<job_dir>/work`). So the producer cannot read the source it is told is "present". Second, a major gap: criterion 7 requires a test that the hook is called at study start. Every test calls the study code directly, so removing the call in run.rs would break no test.
